If rock unit D is an intrusion, which geologic principle would you use to determine the age of rock unit D with respect to rock unit E (the fault)? 

This is a declarative sentence.

To determine the age of rock unit D with respect to rock unit E, we would use the principle of cross-cutting relationships. Since rock unit D is an intrusion, it cuts across rock unit E, which is a pre-existing rock unit. This means that rock unit D is younger than rock unit E, as it was formed after the rocks that make up rock unit E.
